name: branch_point_relocate
title: 3-terminal net: the T junction belongs at the Steiner point
expected_summary: 0 vias, junction at the Fermat point [5.8868, 7.0] (angles [119.9992, 120.0004, 120.0004]), total 22.660 mm. Careless T on the P-Q wire at (3, 7): 24.0 mm (+5.6 %); pad chain 24.87.
why: All three angles of the pad triangle are below 120 degrees (P 72.6, Q 72.6, R 39.8), so the shortest tree has a free branch point where the three wires meet at 120 degrees. No other copper is on the board.

octilinear_note.text: in the 45-degree style the 120 degree junction does not exist; the octilinear optimum (two 45-degree legs from P and Q to a trunk on y = 7, trunk to R) is the same family of answers: junction x = 8.0, length informational, not drawn

interpretation.rule: all three angles < 120: a free branch point at the Fermat point, 120 / 120 / 120 (Popov 2013 EDN; TopoR 5.0 E8c Auto move)

judgement_calls: any-angle (smooth) style is drawn; an octilinear board would use the 45-degree variant (length in the note)

TopoR 5.0 autorouting builds pad-to-pad chains (E3b); its Auto move in FreeStyle moves a pre-routed T to the Fermat point (E8c). The TopoR run therefore pre-routes the careless T and applies Auto move
literature: Popov, Popov 2013, EDN 'Flexible routing' (docs/literature/popov2013-edn-flexible-routing-full.txt): Steiner junctions at < 120 degrees, a pad takes over the junction when an angle is >= 120
TopoR 5.0 black box E8c / E8d (docs/literature/topor50-blackbox-results.md): Auto move puts a free T at the Fermat point (120 / 120 / 120); at an angle >= 125 the junction is deleted into the pad
TopoR 6.3 User Manual (docs/literature/eremex2017-topor63-user-manual.pdf) pp. 175-183: FreeStyle, move vias and T-points, delete extra vias

reference.label: T junction at the Steiner (Fermat) point

careless.label: T junction on the P-Q wire (R joined to the nearest point of the existing wire)

topor: see topor50/ (filled by the TopoR run, if any)
